protocol.instrument_name: Protocol for Management of Acute Exacerbation of Mild Plaque Psoriasis
protocol.legal_basis: Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Act 1981 and the Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Regulations 2017 (the Regulations); supply of the Schedule 4 poisons documented in this Protocol for the purpose of managing acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis under a structured prescribing arrangement; requirement of the Secretary Approval: Community Pharmacist Statewide Pilot that pharmacists comply with this Protocol and have completed the designated pharmacist training requirements specified in the departmental guidance before supplying the Schedule 4 poisons (page 4, '1. About').
protocol.supervision_model: structured prescribing arrangement (document's own term) under the Secretary Approval: Community Pharmacist Statewide Pilot; pharmacists must operate at all times in accordance with the Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Act 1981, the Regulations and all other applicable Victorian, Commonwealth and national laws, and act in a manner consistent with the Pharmacy Board of Australia's Code of Conduct (page 4, '1. About').
protocol.scope_summary: Victorian Community Pharmacist Statewide Pilot protocol (February 2024) authorising supply of Schedule 4 poisons for managing acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis, by resupply of prescription-only topical corticosteroids (TCS) that the patient has used previously for their psoriasis and that are available under the pilot. Contains a flowchart (pages 5-9), documentation requirements (page 10), supplementary assessment guidance (pages 12-13), management guidance (pages 14-15), a Medicines table (page 16) and resources (pages 17-18). Adapted from the draft Clinical Practice Guideline Acute Exacerbations of Mild Plaque Psoriasis from Queensland Health (page 18).

steps.description: CONDUCT CLINICAL REVIEW - Examination: '1. Confirm signs and symptoms including defined raised red, scaly patches, silvery-white scales of skin which shed or flake, dry, cracked skin that may bleed, itching and pain. Patches are typically symmetrical. 2. Complete assessment of severity using PASI and/or DLQI calculator.' Severity branches as printed: 'Moderate to Severe' -> 'Refer to General Practitioner and consider seeking specialist referral where appropriate'; 'Mild' -> continue to patient history. Severity thresholds (page 13): 'Mild plaque psoriasis = a PASI <= 5 and/or DLQI <= 5'; 'Moderate plaque psoriasis = a PASI 6-10 and/or DLQI 6-10'; 'Severe plaque psoriasis = PASI >10 and/or DLQI >10'.

gates.criterion: Severity assessed as Mild (PASI <= 5 and/or DLQI <= 5) - not 'Moderate to Severe'

provenance.section_heading: 2.1. KEY TO COLOURS USED IN THIS PROTOCOL

steps.description: Patient history: '1. medication history including TCS used previously for psoriasis, and any new medications - review MHR as necessary, where possible/available; 2. medical history including complications, pregnancy and/or breastfeeding; 3. aggravating factors; 4. psychological impact'. Supplementary patient-history considerations (page 12, '4.1. PATIENT HISTORY') include age; pregnancy and lactation status, including patients planning pregnancy (if applicable); onset, duration, nature, location, severity and extent of plaques; previous diagnosis and history of exacerbation(s); co-existing and underlying medical conditions including psoriatic comorbidities such as arthritis or depression; response to any previous treatments; impacts on quality of life and psychosocial wellbeing; exposure to factors that can aggravate psoriasis (Table 1); current, recently commenced or recently ceased medications; family history of psoriasis; drug allergies/adverse drug effects.

provenance.section_heading: 2.1. KEY TO COLOURS USED IN THIS PROTOCOL

steps.description: 'Does the patient report / present with any of the following?' - 'The patient has psoriatic comorbidities or risk factors that require management by a medical practitioner e.g., arthritis, risk of venous thromboembolism, depression, increased alcohol consumption, signs of lymphoma, skin cancers and solid tumours'; 'The patient has not seen a medical practitioner for review of their psoriasis in the previous 12 months'. Yes branch -> 'Refer to a medical practitioner', with the printed caveat 'Pharmacotherapy by pharmacist may still be considered if clinically appropriate - go to: PHARMACOTHERAPY section on page 6 below.' No branch -> continue to the next page's exclusion list.

gates.criterion: Patient reports/presents with NONE of the printed items (no psoriatic comorbidities or risk factors requiring medical management; has seen a medical practitioner for review of their psoriasis in the previous 12 months)

provenance.section_heading: 2.1. KEY TO COLOURS USED IN THIS PROTOCOL

steps.description: 'Do any of the following apply?' (12 items, reproduced in eligibility.exclusion EXC-3 to EXC-14): the diagnosis is unclear; patient is very visibly unwell; immunocompromised; other medical conditions such as diabetes or psoriatic arthritis where referral to a rheumatologist may be required; pregnant or planning a pregnancy; type of psoriasis other than mild plaque psoriasis; psoriasis is moderate (PASI 6-10 and/or DLQI 6-10) or severe (PASI >10 and/or DLQI >10) including marked negative emotional and social effect; face, scalp, genitals, palms and/or soles affected; psoriasis covers a significant body surface area (affects more than 6% of the body); psoriatic lesions infected or show pustulation; taking a medicine that can exacerbate, especially lithium, beta-blockers and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs; inadequate response to topical treatment. Yes branch -> 'Refer to General Practitioner and consider seeking specialist referral where appropriate'. No branch -> continue to page 6 (printed; PDF page 8) PHARMACOTHERAPY.

gates.criterion: None of the 12 printed exclusion/referral conditions apply

provenance.section_heading: 2.1. KEY TO COLOURS USED IN THIS PROTOCOL

steps.description: PHARMACOTHERAPY: 'Does the patient have allergies, drug-drug interactions or any other contraindications to treatments under this protocol?' Yes -> 'Where therapy is considered the appropriate treatment option but all recommended treatments under this protocol are contraindicated, refer patient to a medical practitioner'. No -> 'Provide treatment, where indicated* - Resupply of TCS preparation that patient has used previously for their psoriasis and is available under the pilot (see Section 6 for list of medicines that can be supplied under this pilot)'. Section 6 Medicines list (page 16) contains these topical corticosteroids: betamethasone valerate 0.02% and 0.05%, triamcinolone acetonide 0.02%, betamethasone dipropionate 0.05%, betamethasone valerate 0.1%, methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1%, mometasone furoate 0.1% (Moderate and Potent Corticosteroids classes as printed). Printed notes: '* Note that while liquor picis carbonis (LPC, or coal tar solution) +/- keratolytics (e.g., salicylic acid) and calcipotriol are also treatment options for psoriasis, these have not been included for supply and reimbursement in the pilot, which has focused on the resupply of prescription only topical corticosteroids.' (page 8). Page 14: 'NB1: Topical preparations containing LPC and/or salicylic acid (in dermal preparations containing <40% salicylic acid) are also a treatment option for psoriasis and may be sold without a prescription. These have not been included in the pilot however, which has focused on the resupply of prescription only TCS.' 'NB2: TCS are the mainstay of treatment for psoriasis flare. If topical treatment with class I-III TCS does not produce an adequate response to the acute exacerbation, the patient should be referred to a medical practitioner for management.'

gates.criterion: No allergies, drug-drug interactions or any other contraindications to treatments under this protocol

provenance.section_heading: 2.1. KEY TO COLOURS USED IN THIS PROTOCOL

steps.description: Provide non-pharmacological and self-care advice: '1. Provide patient with Consumer Medicines Information and/or a Self-Care Fact card to help patients control their plaque psoriasis; 2. Provide advice on preventing flare-ups i.e., flare-ups can be triggered by stress, cold weather, dry skin, certain foods or drinks; 3. Keep skin moisturised using a soap-free cleanser or wash and apply fragrance-free moisturiser.'

steps.description: Supplementary general advice (page 15): 'Patients should be advised that each new treatment may take time to work and should be trialled for 2 to 4 weeks. However, adequate response to optimal topical treatment may take up to 3 to 6 months to be achieved.' 'If a good response has been achieved, advise the patient to reduce the frequency of TCS application until stopped. The patient can resume their usual management plan. If they experience a further acute exacerbation (flare up) of their psoriasis they can seek another psoriasis consult (for the duration of the Victorian Pilot).' 'The patient should be advised to immediately see their medical practitioner if symptoms worsen after commencing treatment.' 'Common adverse effects of TCS, such as transient burning, stinging or pain on application, can generally be reversed by stopping the medicine. - Referral to a medical practitioner is required when adverse effects cannot be managed in the pharmacy setting.' 'All patients should be advised to contact a medical practitioner if: They are not responding to treatment; and/or Their condition worsens; and/or They are experiencing complications (as soon as the complications become evident).'

open_questions.observed: Page 16 table text extraction yields brand strings containing '1/5' and '1/2' tokens (e.g. 'Antroquoril, Betnovate 1/5, Celestone-M, Cortival 1/5' and 'Betnovate 1/2, Cortival 1/2') and, for the first two rows, a preparations cell reading only 'cream,' immediately followed by the pack cell.

open_questions.topic: Printed page numbers differ from PDF page markers
open_questions.observed: PDF page markers run 1-20 while footers print 'Protocol for Management of Acute Exacerbation of Mild Plaque Psoriasis 1' starting at PDF page 3; flowchart boxes cross-reference printed pages ('Yes: continue to page 4', 'continue to page 5/6'), i.e. printed page = PDF page minus 2.
open_questions.why_unclear: All provenance pages use the === PAGE n === markers as required; consumers replaying the flowchart's own 'continue to page N' instructions must map printed page N to PDF page N+2.

open_questions.topic: Page 6 branch outcome leaves treatment discretion
open_questions.observed: For psoriatic comorbidities/risk factors or no medical review in the previous 12 months the Yes branch prints 'Refer to a medical practitioner' and, beneath it, 'Pharmacotherapy by pharmacist may still be considered if clinically appropriate - go to: PHARMACOTHERAPY section on page 6 below.'
open_questions.why_unclear: Whether supply proceeds at the same consultation when this branch fires is left to clinical judgement; recorded as exclusion EXC-1/EXC-2 with exception EXE-1.

open_questions.topic: No emergency referral pathway in this document
open_questions.observed: Referral destinations printed are General Practitioner, specialist/rheumatologist and 'a medical practitioner'; no emergency department, ambulance or 000 escalation appears in the 20 pages.
open_questions.why_unclear: referral.emergency is empty because the document genuinely contains none (not a transcription gap).

open_questions.observed: referral.routine and referral.urgent quote destinations printed across pages 5, 6, 7, 9, 12, 13 and 15; the shared provenance object references the first page (5).
open_questions.why_unclear: Single shared provenance per schema; page range recorded here as required by the spec.

open_questions.observed: Severity rules are written as 'a PASI 6-10 and/or DLQI 6-10', 'PASI >10 and/or DLQI >10' and 'Mild plaque psoriasis = a PASI <= 5 and/or DLQI <= 5'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The structured form allows only one parameter per red flag, so RF-11 carries the moderate PASI band and RF-12 the DLQI >10 rule; the full OR wording is retained verbatim in trigger_text and in eligibility text. The document does not state how to combine a mild PASI with a moderate DLQI (highest-score rule is not printed for psoriasis, unlike the UKMEC 'highest category' rule in the OCP protocol).
